routes.reason: Accept. The route is typed `new` because ModpRepresentationsOfGL2OverLocalFields is not yet in the atlas, but in substance it is a join, and both the reason and the brief say so: PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-23 proposes the same id with the same title, and this brief ends `The id is the one proposed by the extraction of Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł (2023), so both papers feed one roadmap.' The id is free in the atlas, `langlands` is a galaxy id, and nothing existing owns the mod p theory of GL_2(K) for K not equal to Q_p: PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp is the p-adic theory over Q_p, and SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups is the general smooth theory this brief imports from rather than duplicates. The 52 items are §§5–7, which is the right body of material. One cross-extraction inconsistency to hand to the design job: the two proposals give the roadmap different areas, `langlands` here and `representations` in PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-23. Both are galaxy ids, so neither route is wrong on its own, but one roadmap cannot sit in two galaxies and neither brief reconciles them. I have not changed either, since the choice is the design job's; on the content — Gelfand–Kirillov dimension, Iwasawa algebras, blocks, admissible representations, and on the Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł side finiteness conditions and the ordinary part — `representations` is the better fit.

Accept. A Part II of LocalGaloisDeformationRings whose title reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly, with `langlands` a galaxy id and the id free. The 34 items are §§3.1–4.3: Kisin modules with descent data and the monodromy condition, and the explicit tame potentially Barsotti–Tate deformation rings for one type and for several types at once, including the Tables 1–5 presentations. The parent owns local deformation rings and their components in general; what is added here is the explicit unramified tame potentially Barsotti–Tate case that the patching argument of §8 consumes, which the parent does not reach. The brief's imports — Kisin modules and Breuil–Kisin theory from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory — are the right ones.

Accept. A Part II of HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves whose title reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly, including its Title Case, with `automorphic` a galaxy id and the id free. The 24 items are §8, the global endpoint: patching functors, freeness for types and for projective covers, the Gelfand–Kirillov dimension theorems and the flatness of the dual of completed cohomology over the big Hecke algebra. One correction made in place: the brief listed the final theorems as `Corollaries 8.3.9, 8.4.4, 8.4.6, 8.5.1 and Theorems 8.4.1–8.4.2', repeating the very mislabel that the extraction's own finding E1 records — 8.3.9 is a Theorem, and 8.4.4, 8.4.6 and 8.5.1 are the corollaries. I have moved 8.3.9 to the Theorems list.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-7b31c4, issue #1242, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by Claude Code, sessions cc-442dc5 and cc-d67081 (issue #1241). Source read: arXiv:2009.03127v7, 112 pages, whose recorded sha256 8f06c68bbb85aa3d13420181197167b3ce9158dc117e96da6299718765f99e7a reproduces byte for byte. The second checkpoint's correction of the version label from v4 to v7 is right: the file at that hash is the v7 of 9 June 2023 marked final.

Coverage, checked mechanically and then by hand. I extracted every numbered label of the form Theorem/Proposition/Lemma/Corollary/Definition/Remark/Conjecture N.N.N from the source: 142 distinct ones. All but one are named in an item locator or item name. The exception is 'Theorem 14.8', which is a citation to Breuil-Paskunas inside the proof of Lemma 6.3.7 ('see Theorem 14.8 in loc. cit.'), not a statement of this paper. So every numbered statement of the paper is carried into the extraction. The main theorems of the introduction are all present with their body attributions, and I checked those attributions against the source: Theorem 1.4 = Theorem 6.4.7, Theorem 1.5 = Proposition 6.4.6, Theorem 1.6 = Corollary 5.3.5, Theorem 1.7 = Corollary 7.3.4, Theorem 1.8 = Theorem 8.3.9 (see the finding), Theorem 1.9 = Theorem 8.4.2, Theorem 1.10 = Theorem 8.4.1.

Statements, spot-checked. I read the printed statements of Corollary 5.3.5, Proposition 6.4.6, Theorem 6.4.7, Lemma 8.3.8, Corollary 8.3.10, Theorem 8.3.11, Theorem 8.4.3 and Lemma 3.3.1 against their items. Six of the eight are reproduced faithfully, in some cases verbatim. Two were not, and I corrected them in place.

(1) The item iwahori-mult-one stated the hypothesis as '(i) and (ii) of Theorem 6.4.7'. The paper's Theorem 1.5, which this item is, cites (i) and (ii) of Theorem 1.4, and those are not the same conditions: Theorem 1.4(i) asks for an isomorphism pi^{K_1} = D_0(rbar_v^vee)^{oplus r} of GL_2(k)-representations, while Theorem 6.4.7(i) asks only that JH(soc_K pi) = W(rhobar) up to multiplicity. The extraction's own local-gk item records correctly that 1.4 is the special case of 6.4.7, so the two items contradicted each other. Corrected to Theorem 1.4, with the reason in the item note.

(2) The item graded-iwahori stated only that the graded ring 'is computed explicitly (Theorem 5.3.4); it is not commutative, since I1/Z1 is not uniform'. That is a description, not a statement, and what is consumed downstream is definite: gk-bound lists this item among its prerequisites, and the proof of Corollary 5.3.5 uses the Auslander-regularity, the central regular sequence (h_0, ..., h_{f-1}) and the identification of the quotient with a polynomial ring in 2f variables. I transcribed Theorem 5.3.4's actual content, keeping the non-commutativity remark.

The finding. The extraction records one sourceIssue, E1, and it is confirmed: the introduction prints 'Theorem 1.8 (Corollary 8.3.9)' while the body has 'Theorem 8.3.9' and a separate Corollary 8.3.10, and the introduction itself says the result 'is ultimately proven in Theorem 8.3.9'. I also found the same mislabel repeated inside the extraction, in the brief of route 3, and corrected it there.

Structure. 110 items, all status missing, each routed exactly once; 3 routes, one new and two Part II. Both Part II titles reproduce their parents' atlas titles exactly, all three areas are galaxy ids, and all three roadmap ids are free in data/atlas.json. The new id is co-proposed by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-23, which the route's reason and brief both acknowledge; the two proposals differ in area (langlands here, representations there), which I record on route 1 rather than settle.

Two observations about the census that a design job should know, neither of them a defect.

- There are no library items and no planned items at all. I checked the pinned libraries for the obvious candidates and the all-missing census holds up: the declaration index at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 has no Gelfand-Kirillov dimension, no Lazard theory of uniform pro-p groups, and no Weierstrass preparation for power series over a complete DVR (which is what the proof of Lemma 3.3.1 uses). So nothing here is already in the libraries.
- The job asks that an item which an atlas layer plans should name that layer. This extraction instead names its imports in the route briefs - completed group algebras from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras, smooth representations from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, Kisin modules from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory, patching algebra from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra, global deformation rings from GlobalGaloisDeformations. That is a defensible style and the imports are the right ones, but it means no item carries a layer pointer, so the design jobs will have to read the briefs to find them.

What this review did not do. I did not read all 112 pages line by line: I read the introduction in full, the statements named above with their surrounding argument, and the section structure. I did not compare the published Inventiones text, which is paywalled, and the extraction records the same boundary. I add no finding of my own beyond the two item corrections and the brief correction described above.
